t: You're at the site of St Mary Abbots Hospital on Marloes Road in Kensington, which operated from 1871 to 1992. Several notable people have links to it. The painter and militant suffragette Georgina Brackenbury died here; she was one of Emmeline Pankhurst's pallbearers. Letitia Fairfield, the first female Chief Medical Officer for London, also died here. So did the artists' model Dolores and the solicitor Paget Bowman, co-founder of the British National Opera Company. The businessman and theatre impresario Sir Rupert Gavin was born here.
